notes: reviewed: MockMailbox (contracts/MockMailbox.sol, fee 0) and SpecIsm, which accepts every message (the worst case: any release message, any receiver, any amount)
the handler records every successful lock amount and every successful claim amount (sumLocked / sumReleased)
release delay 0 so a release can be claimed in the step after its message; the daily limit is 10 ETH; the setup locks 5 ETH from 0xB0B (counted in sumLocked)

actions.lock:
ok = call_lock(caller, a);
if (ok) sumLocked += a[2];

harness.views:
function released() external view returns (uint256) { return sumReleased; }
function lockedTotal() external view returns (uint256) { return sumLocked; }

properties.rationale: handle (line 204) reverts on a comparison of msg.sender with mailbox.

properties.title: nonce never decreases
properties.statement: No call, by anyone, with any arguments, makes `nonce` smaller (it is only ever increased: lock).
properties.rationale: every write of nonce is += or ++.
properties.scope: every function that writes nonce, any caller and arguments, from any state reachable in prover.depth-1 steps

properties.title: received never decreases
properties.statement: No call, by anyone, with any arguments, makes `received` smaller (it is only ever increased: handle).
properties.rationale: every write of received is += or ++.
properties.scope: every function that writes received, any caller and arguments, from any state reachable in prover.depth-1 steps

properties.title: the contract always holds at least locked in ETH
properties.statement: After any sequence of calls (by anyone, with any arguments), the contract's ETH balance is at least `locked`: what it owes is always backed (lock add, claim pay out).
properties.rationale: locked grows in payable lock and shrinks where ETH is sent (claim).
properties.scope: bounded: every sequence of prover.depth calls over harness.steps from the setup state (Halmos); unbounded where the SMTChecker proves it; fuzzed by forge

properties.title: pausing loses nothing
properties.statement: `pause` and `unpause` change no balance and no public state except `paused`: the contract's ETH and every public number, address and flag are the same before and after.
properties.rationale: pause writes paused.
properties.scope: from any state reachable in prover.depth-1 steps; public no-argument getters and the ETH balance (mappings are covered by the AST fact that pause writes only the flag)

properties.title: lock is stopped while paused
properties.statement: Once `pause` ran, `lock` reverts for every caller and argument.
properties.rationale: lock reverts on paused.
properties.scope: any caller and arguments, after a pause from any state reachable in prover.depth-1 steps

properties.title: claim is stopped while paused
properties.statement: Once `pause` ran, `claim` reverts for every caller and argument.
properties.rationale: claim reverts on paused.
properties.scope: any caller and arguments, after a pause from any state reachable in prover.depth-1 steps

properties.title: lock: no storage write after an external call
properties.statement: `lock` makes external calls (dispatch with ETH line 186, dispatch with ETH line 185, call with ETH line 190); every storage write happens before the first call.
properties.rationale: a write after an external call lets the callee re-enter while the state is stale (the classic reentrancy pattern).
properties.scope: static: the solc AST of the function, its modifiers and the internal functions it calls

properties.title: claim: no storage write after an external call
properties.statement: `claim` makes external calls (call with ETH line 240); every storage write happens before the first call.
properties.rationale: a write after an external call lets the callee re-enter while the state is stale (the classic reentrancy pattern).
properties.scope: static: the solc AST of the function, its modifiers and the internal functions it calls

properties.title: releases never exceed locks, and locked is exactly locks minus releases
properties.statement: After any sequence of locks, release messages (forged or not: the ISM here accepts everything), claims, pauses and vetoes, the ETH paid out by claims is at most the ETH locked, and `locked` equals locked minus paid. Even a compromised ISM can only release this route's own deposits.
properties.rationale: HyperlaneLockBoxV2's header: 'within what this contract holds for locks (`locked`: locks minus releases), so even a forged message can never take more than this route's own deposits'.
properties.scope: bounded: every sequence of 2 calls over lock, handle (any message), claim, pause, veto from the setup state (5 ETH locked) (Halmos); fuzzed by forge

properties.title: a claim never takes the day's releases over the daily limit
properties.statement: After any successful claim, `releasedToday` is at most `dailyLimit`.
properties.rationale: claim reverts with OverLimit when releasedToday + amount > dailyLimit.
properties.scope: any caller and claim, after any 1 call from the setup state (Halmos)

properties.title: a claim reduces locked by exactly the ETH that left
properties.statement: After any successful claim, `locked` went down by exactly as much as the contract's ETH balance.
properties.rationale: claim: locked -= amount, then pays amount.
properties.scope: any caller and claim, after any 1 call from the setup state (Halmos)
